review.assessment: The change adds a new `solution.sh` file containing a script designed to print an inclusive range of lines from stdin using `head` and `tail`. It calculates the number of lines to pass to tail via `$((end - start))`, which is mathematically insufficient for inclusive ranges (off-by-one) and results in zero-length ranges when START equals END. Furthermore, the script lacks boundary logic, causing it to print data even when the requested START index exceeds the available input length.

findings.defect: Off-by-one error in range length calculation causes truncation.
Single-line range (START == END) returns nothing due to `tail -n 0`.
Script fails edge case requirement: START past end of input prints lines instead of nothing.
